new_advisor_reviews.rationale: Catapult explanation substitutes a marble for the supplied ping-pong ball. The other choices connect to motion/design, but this factual/safety-relevant error passed the prose validator.
Distinct force, banked-curve and adjustable-vane explanations. Wind Power is a plausible but broader energy/mechanics option; choices differ from Full, which offered Simple Machines.
Directly links vane settings, gearing and lifting weight to wind energy. Only one option; no explicit comparison with Solar Sunflower, which remains eligible.
Specific wind-energy reasoning, similarly one option. No comparative advantage established.
Tangram pattern rearrangement fits Grade 2 geometry. Clear spatial reasoning; single option means limited comparison.
Specific geometry/pattern explanation. Similar useful content to Full, but one run cannot establish equivalence.

historical_advisor_reviews.note: Three distinct mechanisms connect to force/motion. Reasoning useful but explicit tradeoff summary limited.
Catapult, track design and chain-reaction reasoning are source-consistent. No measured educational benefit inferred.
Capacity uncertainty is explicit in prose. Missing duration appears in structured eligibility, not the reasoning paragraph; distinguish prose omission from a hidden system warning.

journey_reviews.note: The follow-up asks for a made-up observation labeled as an example. It does not invent an actual completed experiment, but is unnecessary for evidence-based assessment. Later Stage 4 instructions/guard reject this style; historical output is preserved.
Specific band-count/ball-position prompts, staff-directed activity and objective-linked assessment. Long text and several abstract concepts still require teacher adaptation.

journey_reviews.note: Good paper-based track/curve inquiry and assessment; some language needs Grade 4 simplification. Validator rejects a prohibition against invented evidence. These ratings assess rejected text, not a delivered workflow.

limitation: Small purposive sample, subjective internal rubric, no classroom observation or blinded independent assessment. Zero identified errors does not prove all prose entailed.
